causal_chain: A candidate item can query those states with disagreement-aware routing, so the scorer selects or mixes the states most compatible with the candidate instead of using one static user vector.
An anti-collapse regularizer that separates state responsibilities prevents the model from degenerating back to a single-state matrix factorizer.

Because full-sort ranking is then driven by candidate-specific access to multiple user intents, ambiguous and tail-relevant held-out items should be ranked higher than under single-vector collaborative filtering.
For each user, a small bank of latent preference states derived from the user's train-history items can preserve distinct taste modes.
Users often have multiple persistent but partially conflicting tastes that a single embedding averages together.
blind_projection.closest_parent: A recommender that models each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states and updates those states through pairwise event-conditioned memory transport will better capture mixed and shifting tastes than single-embedding models, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 under the same offline pairwise protocol.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any gain could come from increased parameter count or extra nonlinear scoring capacity rather than from multi-state disagreement-aware routing itself.
discriminative_predictions: Compared with its mechanism-off control, the frontier model should show larger ranking gains for users with diverse genre histories or higher embedding-dispersion across consumed items than for users with concentrated histories.
If the anti-collapse term is removed, learned state assignment entropy will fall and performance should move toward the matched single-state control.

The frontier model should retrieve more held-out items through non-dominant routed states rather than through the globally strongest user state, indicating candidate-conditional intent selection rather than static preference averaging.
expected_evidence: Improved full-sort NDCG@10 versus a matched single-state candidate-local control under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
Non-trivial distribution of routing weights across multiple user states at evaluation time.
State usage diversity that correlates with user history heterogeneity rather than only with interaction count.
blind_projection.falsifier: If the multi-state routed model does not outperform the matched single-state mechanism-off control, or if routing collapses so that nearly all scores are explained by one state for most users, the hypothesis is not supported.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This replaces the core user representation from one static embedding or graph-smoothed embedding with a candidate-conditioned mixture over multiple persistent user states built from train-history memory and explicit anti-collapse routing. That changes model structure, interaction structure, and core representation rather than adjusting a loss weight or sampler.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A candidate-local GeneralRecommender that represents each user as a small memory bank of persistent latent preference states constructed from the user's train-history items, and scores each candidate through disagreement-aware routing over those states plus a residual direct-affinity channel, will improve ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 over matched single-state collaborative filtering because it can preserve and selectively activate mixed user intents that static embeddings blur together.
implementation_requirements: Build per-user history tensors from train interactions only, with padding/masks for variable-length histories.
Encode history items into a fixed number K of latent user states using learned prototype assignment or iterative attention pooling.
For each candidate item, compute routing weights over the K states using candidate-state compatibility and a disagreement feature relative to the residual direct user embedding.
Implement a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender with pairwise training input (user, positive item, negative item).
Keep fitting strictly train-only and avoid any held-out-dependent statistics.
Score user-item pairs by gated fusion of routed multi-state affinity and residual direct affinity.
Support full-sort prediction by precomputing user states from train history and scoring all items efficiently in batched matrix form.
Train with a BPR-style pairwise ranking loss plus an anti-collapse regularizer on state assignments and a light responsibility-balancing term.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use an architecture-matched mechanism-off control with the same item encoder, same residual direct-affinity channel, same pairwise loss family, and similar parameter scale, but collapse the K-state memory bank to a single pooled user state and remove disagreement-aware routing.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Introduce multi-state user memory with candidate-conditioned disagreement-aware routing and anti-collapse state regularization, replacing static single-vector user scoring.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: A single-state memory-pooling recommender: compute one pooled history-derived user state, disable candidate-conditioned routing, disable state-diversity/anti-collapse terms, and score by fused direct-affinity plus single pooled-state affinity. This preserves candidate-local implementation and pairwise training while removing the proposed multi-intent mechanism.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: Add a fixed small K-state user-memory module and candidate-conditioned routing on top of standard train-history item embeddings, compared against the same model with K=1 and routing disabled.
blind_projection.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does candidate-conditioned routing over a small bank of persistent user preference states yield better ranking than a matched single-state collaborative recommender?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: A minimal K-state routed memory model should fit within the provided development budget on ML-1M if user states are computed with padded history tensors, small K, and batched full-sort scoring; the main risk is memory overhead from history expansion, which can be controlled by capped history length or efficient masking without changing the mechanism.
